_instructions: Copy this file to my-data/fact_registry.json and fill it in, ideally by running prompts/03_proactive_interrogation.md in an AI chat. Every resume claim must trace to a fact in this file. Delete these _instructions lines as you go. Keep this file PRIVATE.

identity.headline_credential: [Optional: one line for an active clearance or headline certification, if you have one. Otherwise empty.]

career_thesis._instructions: Summarize from your filled career_thesis_template.md. 2 or 3 destination paths.

paths.name: [e.g. People leadership track in your field]

scope.team_size: [number you managed or worked within, or unknown]
scope.budget: [amount you owned or influenced, or none]
scope.customers_or_users: [who your work served, with numbers if known]

facts.claim: [One true statement about what YOU did, in your own words. e.g. Migrated 40 stores to a new point-of-sale system over 6 months with zero days of lost sales.]
facts.evidence: [How you know the numbers: report, email, memory of the project plan.]
facts._source_options: confirmed_by_user | source_resume | walk_through - the fact-check module (07) only accepts claims tracing to one of these

skills_and_tools: [Tools, platforms, methods you have actually used. One entry each.]
metrics_bank: [Standalone numbers you can defend: percentages improved, dollars saved, volumes handled, headcounts, timeframes.]
locked_framings: [Phrasings you have decided on and will not let the AI reword. e.g. how you describe a layoff, a gap, a title that undersold the work. Add these as sessions surface them.]
do_not_claim: [Things adjacent to your work that you did NOT do. Listing them here stops the AI from drifting into them. e.g. 'I supported the budget process but never owned a budget.']
lessons_learned: [Optional running list: what worked and failed in past applications, phrasing that landed, portal quirks you hit.]
